ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $AB$ is the diameter of $\odot O$, and chord $CD\perp AB$. Point $E$ is on the extension of $CA$. Connect $DE$ to intersect $\odot O$ at point $F$, and connect $AF, CF$. If the degree of $\overset{\frown}{BD}$ is $40^\circ$, what is the degree of $\angle AFC$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in Figure 1, connect $OD, AD$, and let $AB$ intersect $CD$ at $H$. \\
Since the degree of $\overset{\frown}{BD}$ is $40^\circ$, \\
therefore $\angle BOD=40^\circ$, \\
therefore $\angle DAB=\frac{1}{2}\angle DOB=20^\circ$, \\
since $AB\perp CD$, \\
therefore $\angle AHD=90^\circ$, \\
therefore $\angle ADH=90^\circ-\angle DAB=70^\circ$, \\
therefore $\angle AFC=\angle ADH=\boxed{70^\circ}$.

Then reason: It is known that the measure of arc BD is 40°. Because diameter AB passes through the center of the circle and is perpendicular to chord CD, AB bisects chord CD and also bisects the corresponding arcs determined by C and D, therefore arc BC = arc BD = 40°. The measure of upper semicircular arc BA is 180°, so arc CA = 180° - 40° = 140°. ∠AFC is an inscribed angle, and the arc it subtends is arc AC not containing F, therefore ∠AFC = 1/2 × 140° = 70°.
